title: Field Operations Standard: Dispatch and Handover of Delivery & Pickup Appointments
content:
Under Delivery & Pickup Appointments, an appointment is dispatched when the vehicle is loaded for delivery or staged for pickup, and completed when the buyer accepts the vehicle at handover. The clauses below apply at each of these stages.

## Clauses

**H1. Dispatch.** An appointment is dispatched only when the purchase order is ready for handover under the purchase handover rules of Vehicle Purchase Agreements. Dispatch means the vehicle is loaded for delivery, or staged at the hub or tower for the booked window. The appointment's status moves from scheduled to dispatched.

**H2. Identity.** At handover the buyer shows a government photo ID when the fulfillment method requires it.

**H3. Buyers present.** Every buyer named on the purchase agreement is present at handover when the method requires it.

**H4. Test drive.** Before accepting the vehicle, the buyer may take a test drive of up to the method's test drive maximum miles.

**H5. Condition report.** When the method requires it, the condition report, with the odometer reading, is signed at handover.

**H6. Contactless handover.** A contactless handover is possible only where the method allows it.

**H7. Trade-in collection.** A trade-in vehicle may be collected at the same appointment only where the method allows it.

**H8. Completion.** The appointment is completed when the buyer accepts the vehicle and the condition report is signed, and the status moves from dispatched to completed. Completing the appointment records the handover on the purchase order.

## Points of judgement

| Situation (hypothetical) | Judgement under this standard |
|---|---|
| The order is not yet ready for handover under the purchase handover rules | The appointment is not dispatched |
| The method requires every named buyer and one co-buyer is absent | The requirement in H3 is not met |
| The method's test drive maximum is 5 miles | A test drive of up to 5 miles may be taken before acceptance, but a test drive of 8 miles is beyond what the method permits |
| The method's test drive maximum is 0 miles | No test drive is taken before acceptance |
| The buyer asks for a contactless handover under a method that does not allow it | Contactless handover is not available |
| The buyer brings a trade-in to an appointment whose method does not allow trade-in collection | The trade-in is not collected at this appointment |

## Notes

- The test drive is something the buyer may take; the standard does not require it.
- Which requirements apply, and the test drive figure, depend on the appointment's fulfillment method.
